transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… hi. I guess I’m here because I’ve been really stressed about something with my dad’s lab results. I know it probably sounds like I’m over-focusing on it, and I don’t want to come across as difficult, but for about a year I’ve felt like parts of his results in the clinic system are being changed or held back.

Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but the chart doesn’t match what I saw before. I’ve been trying to prove it, and it’s just… it’s wearing me down.
Do you believe someone is intentionally changing or hiding your dad’s lab results?

I… yes. I mean, I know that sounds strong, and I’m not trying to accuse anyone without a reason, but it really feels like someone in the clinic system is changing them or holding parts back. For about a year I’ve been trying to prove it, because the chart just doesn’t match what I saw before.

Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, so I know maybe I sound like I’m being difficult, but I can’t shake it. It feels intentional. And it’s been wearing me down.
Have you heard or seen things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, not like hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there, if that’s what you mean. I haven’t noticed anything like that. I know this all probably sounds strange, but it’s more about the records not matching what I saw.
If your dad’s doctors showed you clear proof that the lab results were never changed, would you be able to accept that?

I’d want to say yes, because I know that’s probably the reasonable answer. And I don’t want to seem like I’m refusing to listen.

But… honestly, I don’t know if I could just accept it. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that something in the clinic system was changed or held back, because the chart doesn’t match what I saw. So even if they showed me something, I think part of me would still wonder if I was being shown the complete thing. It’s been really hard to let go of.
Because of this concern about your dad’s lab results, has it caused major problems in your daily life?

Um… I guess it has, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, because I’m still working and trying to handle things normally.

But my family has started leaving me out of some of the appointment planning, which… hurts, honestly. I think they feel like I’ll make it about the lab records. And at work, I get the sense I’m not really being considered for lab supervision anymore because people think I get too confrontational about record issues.

I’m not trying to cause problems. I just… I know it probably looks that way.
Aside from your concern about your dad’s lab results, do you have any other strong beliefs that other people say aren’t true?

No, I don’t think so. Not really.

It’s mostly just this one thing with my dad’s lab results. I know I keep coming back to it, and I’m sorry if that sounds repetitive, but for the past year I’ve been trying to figure out whether someone in the clinic system changed something or left part of the results out. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, and I know they think I should accept that, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I have other beliefs like that. This is the thing that’s been wearing me down.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts seem disorganized or hard to follow?

I don’t think so… not in that way.

People have told me I get stuck on the same point, or that I’m hard to talk to when it comes to the lab records, but I don’t think anyone has said my speech is disorganized. I mean, I try to explain it clearly. Maybe I repeat myself more than I realize, but I don’t think my thoughts are hard to follow generally. Does that make sense?
During this past year, have you had a period of at least several days where you felt unusually high, energized, or needed much less sleep than usual?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had nights where I stayed up worrying or going over things in my head, but not like feeling unusually high or energized.

I wouldn’t say I needed less sleep in a good way, if that makes sense. I’ve mostly just felt stressed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How certain are you that someone changed or hid your dad’s lab results?

I mean… pretty certain. I know that probably sounds intense, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but I’ve been trying for the past year to prove it because the chart just doesn’t match what I saw.

Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—and I understand why they want me to let it go. But I really do believe someone in the clinic system either changed something or held part of the results back. I don’t know how else to explain it. It’s been wearing me down.
For how long have you been convinced that someone changed or hid your dad’s lab results?

Um… about a year, I think. It started around when my dad’s health issues got more complicated and he was having labs and appointments all the time.

I know that sounds like a long time to stay focused on it, but that’s when I first felt like something didn’t add up. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over this past year, have you felt much less interested in being around other people than you used to?

I’m not sure… maybe a little, but I wouldn’t say I stopped wanting to be around people completely or anything like that.

I guess I’ve kept more to myself at times, mostly because I don’t want to keep bothering people or have them think I’m being dramatic. But I still care about people. Does that make sense?
Over the past year, have you felt emotionally flat or like it’s been hard to show your feelings?

I don’t think so… not flat, exactly. I mean, I’ve been stressed and probably quieter sometimes, but I still feel things. I still get upset, I still care, I still react.

Maybe I don’t always show it well because I don’t want people to think I’m falling apart, but I wouldn’t say I’m emotionally numb. Is that kind of what you mean?
Over the past year, have you felt like it’s been hard to motivate yourself to do ordinary things?

Not really, no… I mean, I’ve had days where I’m distracted or stressed, but I still get myself to my phlebotomy shifts, pay my bills, shower, eat, take care of normal stuff.

So I don’t think motivation has been a big problem outside of, you know, everything with my dad’s records. I hope that’s clear.
Over the past year, have people told you that you speak much less than you used to?

I don’t think anyone’s really said that to me, no. I mean, I can be quieter if I’m tired or trying not to make things uncomfortable, but I haven’t had people point out that I’m speaking a lot less than before.

At least… not that I can remember. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt that someone was putting thoughts into your mind?

No… I don’t think anyone is putting thoughts into my mind. That sounds a little different from what I mean.

It’s more that I can’t let go of what I saw with my dad’s lab results. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or held parts of it back, because the chart doesn’t match what I remember seeing. And I know people keep telling me the numbers are fine, my family and doctors, but… I just don’t believe that explains it.

I’m not trying to sound unreasonable. It’s just been wearing me down, and I feel like I need someone to take it seriously.
Did this belief about your dad’s lab results come on suddenly over a few days, or did it build up gradually?

It wasn’t exactly overnight. It kind of built up… I’d look at the chart, and then I’d remember what I saw before, and it just didn’t match. At first I tried to tell myself maybe I was misunderstanding something, but over time I kept coming back to it.

For about the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or held parts of my dad’s lab results back. I know that sounds like a lot, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but even when doctors or my family say the numbers are fine, I still feel like the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s been wearing me down.
Compared with before this started, do you feel your ability to function in daily life has clearly gotten worse overall?

I wouldn’t say it’s clearly gotten worse overall, no. I mean… I know this situation with my dad’s records has taken up a lot of my attention, and I probably talk about it more than people want.

But outside of that, I’m still keeping my phlebotomy shifts, paying my bills, taking care of myself, doing the normal day-to-day things. So I don’t think I’ve, like, fallen apart or anything. Does that answer what you mean?

But outside of that, I’m still keeping my phlebotomy shifts, paying my bills, taking care of myself, doing the normal day-to-day things. So I don’t think I’ve, like, fallen apart or anything. Does that answer what you mean?

inference.note: A single, non-bizarre persecutory delusion has persisted for about a year with otherwise preserved functioning and no hallucinations, disorganization, negative symptoms, mania, or broad deterioration, ruling against F29 and supporting delusional disorder.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient’s main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a single fixed persecutory belief lasting about 1 year that clinic staff are changing or withholding the father's lab results, with high conviction despite repeated reassurance and doubtful ability to accept contrary proof. There are no hallucinations, thought insertion, disorganized speech, prominent negative symptoms, or manic symptoms, and overall functioning is largely preserved outside the impact of the delusional belief. This is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
